# Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene

## Goal

Consume ToneForge reproducibly and ensure no Node-only dependency leaks into the browser game bundle, satisfying the parent epic's pinned-dependency and clean-bundle acceptance criteria.

As the game's developer, I want a reproducible, pinned audio toolchain so builds never silently depend on an unpinned sibling checkout.

## Scope

- Add the ToneForge dependency to the game `package.json` (build-time CLI consumption via `file:` to the sibling checkout, or a git reference pinned to a commit/tag).
- Pin to the resolved commit/tag and record it; the build must not silently depend on a floating checkout.
- Verify the browser bundle contains no Node-only ToneForge modules (`node-web-audio-api`, filesystem/CLI code).
- Add a bundle-hygiene assertion or CI check that fails if a Node-only module is imported into the browser entry graph.
- Confirm the ToneForge licence work (sibling work item) is resolved or tracked as a blocker.
- Record the pinned revision in the build script or a lockfile-adjacent manifest.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `package.json` declares a reproducible ToneForge dependency pinned to a commit or tag (not a floating branch).
- The resolved pinned revision is recorded and referenced by the build.
- The browser bundle contains no Node-only ToneForge module (verified by build inspection).
- An automated check fails if a Node-only module enters the browser entry graph.
- The build succeeds without requiring an unpinned `../ToneForge` checkout beyond the declared dependency.
- The ToneForge licence status is resolved or explicitly recorded as an open blocker.
- `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Dependencies

- Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback.

## Deliverables

- Updated `package.json` with the pinned ToneForge dependency.
- Lockfile update recording the resolved revision.
- Bundle-hygiene check (script or CI assertion).

## Key Files

- `package.json` — dependency declaration and scripts.
- `package-lock.json` — resolved revision.
- `vite.config.ts` — bundle entry configuration.
- `scripts/build-audio.sh` — consumes the pinned CLI.
data.title: Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene

## Problem statement
`npm run capture` produces **no console output for ~20 s** (browser/ Vite startup + 2 s warm-up + 15 s recording + decode), so a normal run looks like a hang. A missing `playwright` devDependency (or its browser) also fails with a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` / Playwright stack instead of an actionable setup step.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I want live progress and an ETA while a capture runs, and a clear preflight error when the capture dependencies are missing, so I can tell a running capture from a hung one and know how to fix setup.

## Desired change
1. Emit startup milestones (headless Chromium launch, game load, PlayScene start, recording start, encoding/probe).
2. During the recording loop, print a periodic (>= every ~2 s) progress line with elapsed / total and an ETA (e.g. a single overwriting line).
3. Preflight the `playwright` import and browser availability; on failure print `Run: npm install && npm run capture:install` and exit non-zero — no raw stack trace.
4. Keep the existing final report on stdout and keep `--json` machine-readable (progress on stderr so stdout stays parseable).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Capture prints distinct startup milestones (browser launch, game load, scene start, recording) as they happen.
2. While recording, progress output shows elapsed/total and a time-to-completion estimate at least every ~2 s.
3. A missing `playwright` package or browser produces a short actionable message naming `npm install && npm run capture:install` and exits non-zero (no `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` stack).
4. Progress goes to stderr; the final human report keeps going to stdout and `--json` remains valid JSON on stdout.
5. Pure formatting/ETA helper(s) are unit-tested; the full project test suite passes.
6. Docs/README updated to mention the progress output and preflight.
data.title: capture: add progress/ETA output and dependency preflight

## Problem statement
The automated gameplay capture spike (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) produces a **silent** clip. Audio was explicitly deferred in the spike; see `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (Known limits -> Audio capture).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I want the generated gameplay video to include the game audio, so demo/attract clips are usable without a separate manual audio pass.

## Desired change
Capture the game audio during `npm run capture` and mux it into the output so the WebM has a synchronised audio track (or explicitly document/prove the chosen alternative).

## Candidate approaches
- **A. Web Audio capture in-page:** resume the game AudioContext on the Enter gesture, route output through a `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode`, combine its track with the canvas video track before `MediaRecorder` (`new MediaStream([...videoTracks, ...audioTracks])`).
- **B. Offline audio + external mux:** reuse the offline WAV pipeline (`npm run build-audio`, `scripts/build-audio.mjs`) and mux the WAV with the captured WebM using a full ffmpeg (the Playwright ffmpeg bundle has no VP9/H.264 decoder, so note the added toolchain requirement).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `npm run capture` produces a video that contains the game audio (audible/verifiable audio track present in the output).
2. The audio capture approach is described in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, including why it works under the browser autoplay policy (user-gesture resume).
3. The produced file's audio presence is verifiable (e.g. an audio track/stream is detected by the browser or a probe), and the capture report records it.
4. Capture remains opt-in/additive: `npm test` and `npm run build` are unaffected.
5. Any new tooling requirement (e.g. a full ffmpeg for muxing) is documented in the known-limits / CI-cost sections.
6. The full project test suite passes.
data.title: capture: include game audio in automated gameplay video

## Pinned ToneForge + bundle hygiene implemented

### Reproducible pin

- **`audio/toneforge/pin.json`** — records the repository (`https://github.com/TheWizardsCode/ToneForge.git`), the exact revision **`5934fb0a0835e8b6ee8297a3a28f51e811b50b0b`** (on `origin/dev`), licence **MIT**, the CLI path and the dependency specifier.
- **`package.json`** — declares the ToneForge dependency as `optionalDependencies.toneforge = "file:../ToneForge"` (the AC-permitted `file:` route). Optional so CI builds without the sibling checkout (verify mode), while the exact revision is pinned by `pin.json`.
- **`package-lock.json`** — records the pinned `file:../ToneForge` entry (v0.1.1, MIT).
- **`scripts/build-audio.mjs`** — loads the pin, verifies `package.json`/`package-lock.json` declare the pinned specifier (fail-closed), logs the pinned revision, and warns if the sibling checkout drifts from the pin.

### Bundle hygiene

- **`scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs`** — recursively scans `dist/` for Node-only markers (`node-web-audio-api`, the ToneForge CLI, `node:fs`/`child_process`/`worker_threads`/`module`/`os`/`crypto`/`url`/`path`) and exits non-zero on any leak.
- Wired into **`npm run build`** (after `vite build`) and the **Pages deploy workflow**; covered by `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.test.ts` (clean pass, leak failure, missing bundle, CLI exit codes).

### Licence

Resolved: `TF-0MUTVQSI6003VPAD` (Update ToneForge licence to MIT) is completed; recorded in `pin.json` as `licence: "MIT"`.

### Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run build` passes with `Bundle hygiene OK — scanned 4 file(s), no Node-only markers`; `npm run build-audio:verify` logs the pinned revision and verifies 49 assets.
- Full suite: **3,166 tests pass** (142 files), including new pin and hygiene tests.
- `npm ci` with the sibling absent (CI scenario) is tolerated (exit 0; ToneForge skipped).

Implementation complete, commit 61a436c5 pushed to dev.

## Delivered (spike POC)
- `npm run capture` — one documented command boots AI_Hell in headless Chromium (Playwright 1.55.1 / Chromium 140 build v1193), starts PlayScene via Enter, drives a deterministic scripted key plan, and writes a playable WebM (VP9) to `capture-output/` (git-ignored). Options: `--duration`, `--output`, `--headed`, `--warmup`, `--port`.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — orchestrator (Vite dev server, real WebGL via `--enable-unsafe-swiftshader`, `canvas.captureStream(60)` + `MediaRecorder`, chunk streaming to Node, in-page probe of the produced video).
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — deterministic sweep plan (`buildScriptedPlan`) plus the `isNonTrivialClip` predicate. Unit-tested in `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` (19 tests).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — recommendation, exact commands/versions, rejected alternatives (B CDP screencast, C renderer.snapshot loop, D deterministic replay), and known limits.
- README pointer added; `.gitignore` ignores `capture-output/`; `playwright` devDependency + `capture`/`capture:install` scripts.

## Evidence (12 s run on 2026-10-06)
- Output: 960x540, WebM/VP9, ~3.5 MiB, ~12.8 s, renderer WebKit WebGL (software).
- Probe: 1.3-2.2% non-black pixels, 564-1161 distinct colours, non-zero frame motion; `nonTrivial: true`; **0 page errors**. Frames decoded back through a `<video>` element confirm the ship/enemies/HUD move over the clip.

## Assumptions / limits (documented)
- Approach A chosen per the work item preference; headless WebGL works via SwiftShader.
- Audio is explicitly **deferred** (silent clip); path to add it recorded in the doc.
- Output is WebM only — no full ffmpeg on PATH and the Playwright ffmpeg bundle has no VP9/H.264 decoder, so no MP4 transcode.
- Runs are not yet frame-reproducible (unseeded wave/spawn RNG); bot input is identical run to run.
- Fully opt-in: capture code lives under `scripts/`, never imported by `src/`; `npm test` / `npm run build` unchanged.

## Verification
- Full suite via the test-skill runner (`--scope full`): **141 files / 3155 tests passed**, cached for audit.
- `npm run build` (build-audio + tsc --noEmit + vite build) passed.

## Measured CI cost
- Browser download ~278 MiB (174 MiB chromium + 104 MiB headless shell), ~915 MiB on disk.
- 12 s clip encodes in ~18 s wall clock, peak RSS ~500 MB. Recommended as an opt-in job, never part of `npm test`.
